title: Policy parsing migration harness + compatibility runway for region/tier routing rules
creator: Priya Narayanan
description:
Problem: Our current routing rule ingestion mixes parsing, validation, and runtime semantics. This has caused subtle incompatibilities when rolling out new configuration features (region selection heuristics, tier-aware fallback weights, and variant substitutions). Several teams have worked around this with ad-hoc checks and downstream guards, which increases cognitive load and makes canaries brittle.

Goal: Replace the monolithic policy intake path with a migration harness that separates: (1) a backward-compatible parser for existing DSL/config, (2) a staged compatibility layer that emits deprecation diagnostics and autofixes where safe, and (3) a strict schema validator used for opt-in "strict mode" validation in Continuous Integration. The harness should let us: ship new rule language constructs, run progressive rollout of compatibility checks, and run golden-file regression tests to ensure no change alters routing decisions for pinned customers.

Scope: This ticket implements the parsing + compatibility runway and the test harness. Runtime execution (router dispatch) will remain unchanged except for adding a runtime compatibility flag to enable the strict schema check before deploy. Separate follow-up tickets will (a) integrate the new schema into the route compiler and (b) wire the canary gating to Console rollouts.

Design decisions considered:
- Option A: In-place strict migration (fast but high risk). Rejected because it forces immediate fixes across many manifests.
- Option B: Dual-driver approach (parser emits both V1 AST and V2 typed IR). Accepted: it allows a gradual shift with runtime feature flags and golden-file comparisons.
- Option C: Runtime-only shims (cheap). Rejected due to limited static signal for developer tooling and CI enforcement.

Key deliverables:
- A new parser module that outputs a normalized AST and a V2 typed representation (with minimal semantic changes).
- A compatibility reporter that classifies findings into: safe-autofix, warning (non-blocking), and error (blocking when strict mode enabled).
- A migration harness that runs over our policy corpus, emits suggested fixes, and writes golden JSON artifacts for CI diffing.
- Integration tests that assert deterministic routing decisions for a selected set of customer manifests (golden-file set).
- Documentation for Console UX and guidance for customers on migrating configs.

Rollout plan:
1) Land parser + harness behind feature flag; run internal corpus and collect diagnostics (this ticket).
2) Publish autofix suggestions to team's migration reports and enable CI checks for internal manifests.
3) Gradually enable strict mode for new repos and for high-confidence config paths.
4) When confidence is high (no regressions in 4 weeks), enable for all internal test runs and offer an opt-in for customers via Console.

Risks and mitigations:
- False-positive blocking errors: mitigate with safe-autofix and non-blocking warnings initially.
- Golden-file maintenance overhead: build tooling to auto-accept identical diffs and to annotate intentional semantic changes.
- SLO regressions during rollout: add smoke-canary that runs a sample traffic replay and checks end-to-end routing metrics (latency and error-rate).

Success metrics:
- 0 routing decision regressions across the golden corpus for two consecutive weeks after enabling the parser.
- Reduction in runtime-mismatch incidents related to policy changes by 80% over 3 months.
- Migration autofix adoption of at least 60% for internal manifests within 6 weeks.
acceptance_criteria: New parser module that produces normalized AST and typed V2 representation checked into repo
Compatibility reporter that categorizes diagnostics into safe-autofix, warning, and error
Migration harness that runs across internal policy corpus and emits golden JSON artifacts
CI job that diffs golden artifacts and fails only when strict mode is enabled
Integration tests that assert no routing decision changes for 20 selected customer manifests
Documentation page with migration guide and console UX mockups linked from ticket
updates: 2025-02-04: Kickoff meeting with runtime, console, and product — agreed on dual-driver approach and feature-flag gating (notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Routing/Parser+Migration+Kickoff).
2025-02-07: Prototype parser landed in experimental/parser branch. Proof-of-concept shows translation of ~95% of existing DSL constructs to V2 IR with stable semantics.
2025-02-10: Compatibility reporter POC added; initial run produced 312 warnings and 18 auto-fix candidates across internal corpus.
2025-02-14: Design review with PM and Console team — decided to expose diagnostics in Console migration tab; created Console mockups (drive link in Links).
2025-02-18: Added golden-file harness and three end-to-end integration tests (GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1148).
2025-02-20: Switched ticket to In Progress and started writing CI wrapper for strict-mode gating.
comments: Maya Chen (Design): We need a clear way to show autofix suggestions in Console without overwhelming users. Recommended prioritizing fixes by safety score.

Liam O'Connor (Assignee): Working on the parser tests and golden-file canonicalization. Plan to add a checksum-based acceptance to speed CI.
